TABLE 11.1 Normal Telemetry Parameters (source: UNC Eshelman School of Pharmacy, 2023) 
There are certain telemetry changes in which nutritional issues and electrolyte abnormalities are often the primary 
cause. Common examples include: 
• Long QT syndrome—when the QT interval is greater than 0.47 seconds in males and 0.48 seconds in females. 
This can lead to life-threatening dysrhythmias and can be caused by low levels of potassium, magnesium, or 
calcium. 
• Torsades de pointes—a life-threatening dysrhythmia known as a multifocal ventricular tachycardia, caused by 
low levels of magnesium (Cohagan & Brandis, 2022). 
• A peaked or mountain T wave illustrates hyperkalemia (high levels of potassium in the blood) (Bord, 2022).
